answer: A sponsor carries 22% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. Because the shale liability is recorded in the trellis ledger at admission, the ridge audit publishes the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must hence place its own capital behind every alias it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. That is 20 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
